title: Correlation register — recomputed from official rows, with n and a legitimacy verdict

inputs.ngs: origination/data/raw-ngs-passing-transcription.txt + data/ngs-passing-2026-week9.json: 240 official QB rows, 240 joined to a game, 0 unjoined
inputs.ngs_weeks_captured: weeks 1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 (week 2 was never captured; NGS lists only passers above its own attempt threshold, so some team-games have no row)

rules.n: n_independent is the number of independent units. Where a row is nested inside a game, the game is the unit and n_independent is smaller than n_rows.
rules.family: The family below is every correlation this file computes. A family defined after seeing the data is itself a selection, and both Holm and BH are shown.
rules.legitimacy: LEGITIMATE / DUPLICATE / ILLEGITIMATE / INSUFFICIENT, with the reason.

correlations.pair: Home points vs away points, same game
correlations.why: One observation per game; no reuse. n is the number of games.
correlations.use: Team-total combos: if ~0, the two team totals can be priced separately.
correlations.reconciliation: AGREES EXACTLY with the published value

correlations.pair: QB passing yards vs his own team's points
correlations.unit: one game (a QB-game row is nested inside a game)
correlations.why: n is published as the number of QB-games (240), but the independent unit is the game (120 games). 117 of those games contribute two QB rows that share the same team points, game total and margin, so they are not independent observations. The point estimate is unaffected; the published significance is overstated because the denominator is inflated by about 2.00x. This file therefore quotes the game-level n and the wider interval it implies.
correlations.reconciliation: SAMPLE DIFFERS — see n_rows vs the published 204; same direction and materially the same magnitude, but the published sample composition is not reproducible from the committed NGS transcription
correlations.note: Partly tautological: a team's points are scored by its offence and passing yards are a component of that offence. The coefficient measures shared cause, not a dependence that can be traded, because the two legs are not independent events in a book's settlement.
correlations.use: QB-yards prop combined with a team-total leg.

combination_products.data_needed: one calibrated probability and one price
combination_products.data_available: probability: yes (model). price: NO — no official source publishes one.
combination_products.verdict: BLOCKED ON PRICE, not on correlation.

combination_products.product: Parlay — two legs in different games
combination_products.joint_probability_rule: P = p1 * p2 (independent games). Verified in-sample: C1 = 0.0760, consistent with independence in the extreme tails of a team total.
combination_products.data_needed: two prices and a joint settlement rule
combination_products.vig_note: At an assumed -110 per leg, a 2-leg parlay pays 2.6446 decimal (1.90909^2). Break-even joint probability is 0.2744, i.e. each leg must win 0.5238 at the same rate as a single. A parlay does not create edge; it multiplies stake variance by roughly 2x for the same expected value.
combination_products.verdict: CORRELATION IS DEFENSIBLE; ECONOMICS ARE WORSE THAN A SINGLE.

combination_products.joint_probability_rule: P = 1/4 + asin(rho)/(2*pi) for two binary events that are each 50/50 and jointly normal with correlation rho. rho here is C2 = -0.2249, giving P = 0.2139 (independence would say 0.25).
combination_products.data_needed: a verified joint outcome per game and two prices
combination_products.data_available: joint outcomes: yes, from official finals. prices: NO.
combination_products.verdict: CORRELATION IS MANDATORY AND IS BEING HANDLED; the product cannot be priced. The correction moves the fair joint probability by only a few points, which is far smaller than the price uncertainty created by having no price at all.

combination_products.product: Player-prop combo — QB yards with his team's total
combination_products.joint_probability_rule: Requires the copula of two continuous variables, not a Pearson r on their means. Pearson r on levels (C5 = 0.4379) does not give the probability that both exceed their lines.
combination_products.data_needed: player-level closing lines and a player-game log with final lines
combination_products.data_available: player-game log: partial (NGS, qualified QBs only). lines: NO.
combination_products.verdict: NOT COMPUTABLE. A level correlation is the wrong object for a joint over/under.

the_two_findings_that_matter: The published n for C5-C8 is the number of QB-games (204 as published, 240 in the full committed transcription), not the number of games. Both QBs in a game share the same team points, total and margin, so those rows are not independent and the published significance is overstated. This file quotes game-level n.
C2, C3 and C4 are three statements about the same residuals, not three findings. Counting them separately inflates the family and quietly weakens every correction that is applied to it.
summary.honest_statement: No correlation in this file can price a bet, because none of them comes with a market line to compare against. The two NGS coefficients that survive a family correction (C5, C6) are also the two most tautological pairs in the register: passing yards are part of the same offence that scores the points. A high, significant, useless number is the clearest example in this repository of what 'correlation only from officially sourced numbers, with n' does and does not buy.

caveats: NGS rows are weekly single-game captures, not a season-long player log. A prop model trained on them inherits that coverage limit (already flagged by the previous session).
Pearson r on levels is sensitive to a few extreme games; no robust regression is claimed. Trimmed values were not substituted, because substituting would be a choice.
The family size is this file's own choice. Adding or removing a pair changes every adjusted p-value, which is why both Holm and BH are published.
